title: Ace settings
description: Settings for how Ace behaves in this project, in ace/config.json. A missing file or a missing key uses the default. Adapters say how this project does a job. These settings say how much agents do on their own, and which optional Ace features are on.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, so your editor checks the file and explains each key.

autonomy.description: How much agents do without a person, in one setting. It sets who_sets_ready and review.fixes. A key you set yourself wins over it.
enumDescriptions: A person sets every ticket ready, and the review fixes nothing: who_sets_ready person, review.fixes none.
A person sets every ticket ready, and the review fixes what has one clearly correct fix: who_sets_ready person, review.fixes simple-only.
Tickets from a plan a person approved go ready on their own, and the review also picks a fix when several are reasonable: who_sets_ready planning-agents, review.fixes all.

ticket_tracker.description: Where tickets live. A built-in tracker needs no ace/TICKET_TRACKER.md. That file, when it exists, replaces single sections of the built-in tracker.
enumDescriptions: No ticket tracker. Skills write a ticket into the reply instead of opening it.
GitHub Issues, through the gh CLI. Ace ships how to read, open, and update tickets.
Another tracker, such as Linear or Jira. ace/TICKET_TRACKER.md says how to use it.

who_starts_runs.description: What starts an agent run, besides a person typing. Ace writes no runner config: the user sets up the runner, such as a CI job or a cloud agent on a schedule, and ace-setup cycle describes it in ace/CYCLE.md.
enumDescriptions: A person starts every run, and ace-mode names the next step.
The user's own runner, such as a CI job or a cloud agent on a schedule. ace/CYCLE.md says what it starts.

who_sets_ready.description: Who moves a new ticket from needs-dev to ready. Without this key, autonomy sets it. A ready ticket is one an agent may build, such as ace-work-ticket on a schedule. A ticket that ace-work-ticket sends back to needs-dev always waits for a person.
enumDescriptions: Only a person. Every ticket an agent opens stays in needs-dev until a person reads it and sets it ready.
The planning skills, ace-grill and ace-to-ticket, set the tickets they write ready, because a person settled and approved that plan with them. Tickets from ace-audit still wait for a person.
Every skill that opens a ticket sets it ready, ace-audit included. Nobody reads a ticket before an agent builds it.

review.description: How the review runs and which findings it fixes on its own. A review is best run by a model other than the one that built the change. ace-review runs three checks: spec (does the change do what its ticket asked), standards (the coding standards), and code (logic, security, performance, and architecture), plus each custom check in ace/checks/.

require_other_model.description: When true, a session never reviews a change it built: it gives the line to send to another model, such as a new session on a different model or the user's runner. When false, it reviews the change on request and adds a one-line tip that a different model catches more.

agents.description: How many agents run the checks of one review. Fixes are always made by one agent, so edits never collide.
enumDescriptions: One agent runs the spec, standards, and code checks one after another.
Each check runs in its own fresh sub-agent, so one check's reading does not sway the next. Costs more. A harness that cannot start sub-agents runs the checks in one agent and says so.

fixes.description: Which findings the review fixes itself. Without this key, autonomy sets it. On a pull request it commits the fixes and pushes them to its branch. On a local diff it leaves them uncommitted.
enumDescriptions: Change no file. Every fix is written as a finding with its best fix, for a person or the implementing agent.
Fix a finding when one edit is clearly correct and a teammate would not have to choose.

Also fix a finding with several reasonable fixes, with the one the reviewer judges best. A fix that changes a product decision, a public contract, or stored data, and every spec and architecture finding, stays a finding.

fix_severities.description: Only findings with one of these severities get fixed. The rest are written as findings. With fixes set to none, this does nothing.

enumDescriptions: You would ask a teammate to change it.
Small, concrete, and worth the author's time.

write_adrs.description: Record architecture decisions in ace/adrs/. When true, ace-grill writes an ADR for each settled decision that is hard to reverse, surprising without its context, and the result of a real trade-off. ace-explain and ace-implement read ADRs whenever ace/adrs/ exists, whatever this says.

max_tickets_per_audit_domain.description: The most tickets one ace-audit pass files for one domain, such as security. It is a cap, not a quota: a pass that finds nothing worth filing files nothing.
